**Coding-standards review**

Reviewed `smartcontractkit/chainlink#23878` against `.github/copilot-instructions.md` at `eaa743b150ca`.

1 inline finding(s).

comments.body:
**High**

a failed capability-side unregistration is never retried and the state needed to retry it is dropped: when `Unregister` fails (`failCount > 0`, line 264-265) the entry stays with `unregistered=false`, but callers only log the error (handler.go:1052-1054, handler.go:1187-1189) and `releaseWhenDrained` unconditionally `deleteIf`s the entry and frees the slot as soon as the cancelled readers drain, after which every future `UnregisterTriggers` returns `ErrWorkflowNotCoordinated` (line 244-247) and even `close()`'s `pending()` snapshot can no longer see the workflow — so the contract at coordinator.go:67 ("A failed capability unregistration is returned and retried on the next call") cannot be honored; failure scenario: pausing/deleting a workflow while a trigger capability is briefly unreachable (gRPC error) leaves the trigger registered on the capability for the life of the node, and the capability keeps firing events into a channel no reader will ever consume (the coordinator never closes the event channel); the same gap hits `RegisterTriggers`'s pre-unregister (line 176-178), which proceeds to re-register under the same registration IDs despite its own comment that the leftover "must be unregistered first: unregistering it later would remove this one" - error is

**Standard:** "handled once, at the layer that can act on it"

**Fix:** have the release waiter (and/or `close()`) retry the capability-side `Unregister` with backoff for entries whose `unregistered` flag is still false — keep such entries out of `deleteIf` until the unregister succeeds — and make `RegisterTriggers` abort (or block) when its pre-unregister fails instead of registering over the leftover
